rationale: div2_clk_q is a single q<=~q toggle on clk_sys (divide-by-2), but intent.sdc:3 declares clk_div4 on it with -divide_by 4 from clk_sys: CST-013 ERROR Established factor mismatch. CDC-002/CDC-030 co-fire as disclosure, not the seeded defect. Reader A's no-reset note does not affect the label: CST-013 traces the toggle structure and no --deck cdc rule triggers on the unreset divider (RDC-025 is outside the deck).

author_reading.rationale: RTL divider is a single toggle flop (divide by 2) but the SDC declares a divide-by-4 generated clock on it: proven divide-factor mismatch.

labels.rationale: The sole clk_sys edge update inverts div2_clk_q, giving divide-by-two once initialized. The generated-clock declaration binds the same register with divide-by-four.
labels.suspected_flaw: The divider has no reset or initializer, so it stays X from default four-state startup.

labels.rationale: In design.sv:9, div2_clk_q is a single toggle flip-flop (div2_clk_q <= ~div2_clk_q) clocked by clk_sys, implementing a divide-by-2 clock. However, intent.sdc:3 declares create_generated_clock clk_div4 on div2_clk_q with -divide_by 4 from clk_sys, which provably contradicts the RTL divide-by-2 derivation (CST-013 ERROR Established).
